answers.suggestions: Spell out the order of simultaneous Day shots and whether a shooter's shot still resolves if the shooter dies in the same round. Reword the block-result message to say plainly that the block succeeded. Show the remaining speaking budget and the current price multiplier in the turn prompt. Consider a short, secret Day channel for Yakuza, or a rule about who can see PMs. Show the number of living players who are Yakuza, Village and Neutral in the Day summary, since that would help the town and the Yakuza plan votes.

answers.confusing_rules: Sniper timing when the shooter dies before the round ends. R25 says a day action doesn't take effect if its user died since taking it, but the Sniper text only covers a dead target. I had to infer from R25 that my Strong shot on Dave would not fire after Dave's Standard shot killed me. Also unclear: whether a Standard shot that kills the shooter resolves before the shooter's own queued shot.
answers.missing_information: As a dead Sniper I could not see the other Sniper claimant's token count or whether his claimed spending matched reality. The round-end resolution order for multiple shots was not shown, so I could not tell which shots had fired. Night-chat contents were hidden from me, which made it hard to judge the Yakuza pattern.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: Once dead, I could not answer public accusations, such as Dave calling my will false. I could not update my will after the Day 2 shot resolved, so the town read the version I wrote before dying.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: The Day log repeats the full claim and vote block for each speaker, and the ledger repeats the same claims again. This is long and makes real events hard to follow. Nothing else looked inconsistent with the rules: the Pharmacist block on Alice, Alice's blocked protection, Erin's track result and the Jester's revenge all matched R9, R23 and R24.
answers.suggestions: Show each Day's events once, with public claims listed separately from chat. Add a line for the Sniper shot queue (target, and whether the shooter died first) so Snipers see the outcome without inferring it. Show the speaking budget left in the Day summary as well as in the turn prompt.

answers.confusing_rules:
1. Two Day shots in the same round (Day 2). Dave shot Heidi (Standard) and Heidi shot Dave (Strong) on their own turns in the same round. R25 says a day action "takes effect when that round of turns ends" and lapses "if you died since taking it". It doesn't say whether all of a round's day actions resolve together, like night actions under R10, or one after another in turn order. I resolved them one after another: Dave's shot killed Heidi, so her shot never fired. If they had resolved together, both would have died, since Dave had Defense None against a Strong attack. That would have changed the whole game. The rules need to state this explicitly.
2. Token refunds for a shot that lapses because the shooter died. The Sniper text only refunds tokens when the *target* died first. R21's "any token spent is gone either way" covers night effects only. So it's unclear whether Heidi's 3 tokens were spent. It didn't matter because she was dead, but the rule is undefined.
3. Who can be hit by the Jester's revenge. "A random Guilty voter from your trial who was alive when that night began." Bob voted Guilty on himself (6 of 6), so the dead Jester is a Guilty voter. He is excluded by the "alive" clause, but it took a careful read to be sure. It's worth saying explicitly.
4. R9 says a role-blocker learns "only whether the block failed". I worded this differently on Night 2 ("did not fail: Alice can be role-blocked") and Night 3 ("was not resisted"). A fixed template would help.
answers.missing_information:
- An explicit, ordered queue of the day actions waiting to resolve in the current round. I had to reconstruct it from chat to decide Dave's and Heidi's shots.
- A ready list of eligible revenge targets (the Guilty voters from the Jester's trial who are alive at the start of the night). I had to derive it by hand from secret votes.
- Each player's token counts, especially after shots fired or lapsed during the Day.
- Whether the "X sent Y a private message" notice was actually shown to the other players. The log only shows Frank's Day 2 PM and Grace's Day 4 PM to Frank as "(to Frank, Grace)", with no public notice line. I couldn't confirm that R4's visibility rule was carried out.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
- Announce that a second shot was attempted but lapsed ("someone tried to shoot Dave, but the shooter died first"), or at least confirm it privately to Heidi's slot. The rules give no wording for this, so the public only saw "someone shot at Heidi". Dave publicly stated a fact ("Heidi's Strong shot never fired") that he could only infer.
- Check claims in the ledger. Grace's Day 3 and Day 4 claims say "D2: nominated Dave", but Frank was the nominator. Lying is allowed, but a ledger claim that contradicts a public event is worth noting.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
- The ordering of the two Day 2 shots described above. The outcome depended on a resolution order the rules don't define, and only one "A shot rings out" was announced.
- Heidi was told "0 sniper tokens left" when she took the shot, even though it never fired. Under the Sniper's own refund logic this was arguably wrong or at least premature.
- No public notice appears in the log for Frank's and Grace's private messages (R4 says everyone sees that a PM was sent).
- My two role-block results to Grace used inconsistent wording.
- Everything else checked out: role-blocked Alice showed no visit to Erin's track; Carol got her Night 3 result even though she died that night (R10); Bob, the Jester, was correctly named on hanging and won while dead; the game ended correctly when only Frank and Grace (both Yakuza) were left.
answers.suggestions:
- Add a clause to R25: "All day actions taken in the same round resolve simultaneously; a player who dies at that round's end still has their action take effect." Or, if the intent is turn order, state that instead. Also state what happens to the tokens when a shot lapses because the shooter died.
- Give the moderator a "pending day actions" panel and an automatic resolver for them.
- Auto-compute the Jester's and Executioner's revenge targets.
- Use fixed result templates for blockers, protectors and attackers.
- Emit the public "A sent B a private message" event automatically, and show it in the moderator's log.
- Optionally announce a lapsed day action, so players don't have to infer it.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza with a Pharmacist or other blocker
lessons.tip: Before a Katana attack, block the most likely protector (the Medic) in the same night. Blocking Alice on Nights 2 and 3 let the Katana kill Erin and then Carol through a Standard protection that was otherwise active. Confirm the block target and Katana target in night chat before submitting.

A self-nominating claimant who pushes for a vote and then reads Evil on a claimed Village role may be the Jester. Hanging a Jester wins them the game and their revenge kills a random Guilty voter, which can remove a Village power role. Plan around that: Yakuza can let a Jester hang and then count on the revenge.

Kill the investigator whose already-posted result is least useful to you, but kill the Tracker or Sheriff whose next night result could still expose you. Erin (Tracker, who could confirm the Katana visit) and Carol (Sheriff, with a posted Evil read) were killed in order of threat.

Once the living count reaches two versus one Village player, a successful hang on that player ends the game for the Yakuza. Count the parity state before pushing a vote, because each hang or kill is decisive at that point.

Public Sniper claims that conflict (two Snipers) were handled by a shot that killed one claimant. Log every Day shot and its timing, because a shot that kills a player before round end cancels the other shot and its tokens return.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed attack, block or kill the likely protector before retrying.
tips_feedback.why: Blocking Alice (Medic) on Night 3 let the Katana kill Carol, after Carol's Standard protection was otherwise active.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's future results narrow your team (Census Taker, Cartographer, Fortune Teller) before someone whose result is already posted.
tips_feedback.why: Erin's Tracker result could have caught the Katana visit, and killing her on Night 2 removed that threat. Carol was killed after her posted Bob result, which was the next most dangerous.

tips_feedback.tip: Confirm the Katana holder and target in night chat and submit exactly that; with two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill.
tips_feedback.why: Frank and I agreed each night in night chat and submitted the same holder, target and block, so every Katana attack landed and the block landed on the intended Medic.

tips_feedback.tip: Avoid announcing tonight's target or that you will act, publicly or by PM.
tips_feedback.why: We did not announce our nightly plan publicly, so the Village only learned of the Katana attacks after the deaths and could not block them.

output.reason: Filled the lessons and tips_feedback fields from what happened in this completed game; other fields left empty as requested.

reasoning:
I need to put together a StructuredOutput covering lessons and tips_feedback now that the game has concluded, with Yakuza and the Jester winning. As Grace, the Yakuza Pharmacist, I'm reflecting on how the Katana's targeted kills of Erin (Tracker) and Carol (Sheriff) were decisive for the Yakuza's coordinated success.

I'm also noting that blocking a Medic before the Katana attack is a strong strategic pattern worth highlighting, and that Bob's success as Jester -- by claiming Seer and provoking votes to get himself hanged -- shows that Yakuza could exploit a self-nominating claimant as a route to a hang.

Reaching parity and then hanging the last Village member secures the win, which is what happened with Dave on Day 4. Reviewing the tips, "narrow your team before someone's result is posted" and "block the likely protector after a failed attack" both proved useful, while "confirm the Katana holder and target in night chat" also helped coordination.

One notable lesson is that when a Jester gets hanged, their revenge kill can randomly remove a Village player, which indirectly benefits Yakuza — worth remembering for future games. I'll fill in the lessons and tips feedback sections while leaving the other structured output fields empty.

notepad_after: Day 4: Alive are Dave (Village, Sniper claim), Frank (Yakuza, Katana holder), me (Grace, Yakuza Pharmacist). Nominating Dave now: 2 Yes needed; trial needs 2 Guilty of 3. If Dave is hanged, Yakuza win. Otherwise Katana kills Dave at night.

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: A Day shot on a player whose role claim conflicts with yours is not a test. Two real Snipers can exist, and a Sniper's claim can only be checked by your own role knowledge. Shooting a claimant kills a real Village player when the other claim was true, so spend the token on a mechanical read (a Sheriff or Tracker result that conflicts with the target), not on a claim clash.

Track which claimant's protections or results get blocked each night. When a Medic is role-blocked on the same target that later dies to the Katana, the blocker is a living Yakuza candidate. If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Don't publicly announce your protection target. Once Carol's protection was public, the Yakuza's Pharmacist blocked me on consecutive nights and Carol died to the Katana. A block result tells you a blocker is alive, so switch to a less obvious target or hold the protection until you know who the blocker is.

Self-protection doesn't beat a role-block. Spending tokens on yourself only helps if no Pharmacist or Party Animal is alive to block you. Plan for blocks: keep a second likely target in mind and don't assume the claimed target is safe.

A player who nominates themselves and says 'test me' without a second check may be a Jester. A Jester hanged during a Day wins, so before voting Guilty on a self-nominee, ask whether hanging them is what they want.

Track pairs of players whose votes always match, including on nominations. Frank and Grace voted identically on every trial and nomination, and both posted Vanilla Villager claims with no results. A pair like that is a lead to test, not a reassurance.

If the nominee could be a Jester, remember that its revenge kills a random Guilty voter. When every living player votes Guilty, the revenge can hit a power role, so vote Innocent on weak evidence even if you think the nominee is Evil.

tips_feedback.tip: Before a hang, ask whether the nominee wants it (self-nominations, reckless lies).
tips_feedback.why: The tip is right that a player who wants the hang may be a Jester, but I read Bob's self-nominations as a reason to vote Guilty. That is the warning reversed. Bob was the Jester, won by being hanged, and Village lost a hang.

summary: The Yakuza (Frank, a Grunt holding the Katana, and Grace, a Pharmacist) won with the Jester, mostly because the Village kept hurting itself. On Day 2 there were two real Village Snipers, Dave and Heidi. Dave said out loud that "there are two Snipers" was possible, then shot Heidi anyway, and Heidi fired her Strong shot back at a player the Sheriff had cleared. Dave's shot resolved first, so the Village lost a Sniper in the first round of play. Frank then nominated Dave. With Bob, the Jester, the Yakuza had 3 Guilty votes, and Dave survived 4-3 only because Carol's Night 1 Not Evil check had been backed up by Erin's track. The Yakuza played cleanly at night. They agreed every holder and target in night chat, and Grace blocked Alice, the Medic, on Night 2 and Night 3. Alice was easy to predict because she protected Carol every night. That let the Katana kill Erin (Tracker) and then Carol (Sheriff). The worst mistake came on Day 3. Bob claimed Seer, had nominated himself twice, refused to use his last token, and read Evil to Carol, who even said he could be a Jester. Even so, all 6 players voted Guilty. The hang went to a Jester while the Katana was still killing, and Bob's revenge killed Alice that night along with the Katana kill on Carol. Day 4 opened with 3 players alive: Dave and both Yakuza. The Yakuza had a voting majority and hanged Dave, who died with his last Sniper token unused. Carol never checked Frank or Grace, even though they had nominated and voted Guilty on the player she had cleared. She spent Night 3 re-checking Dave instead.

If you do hang, keep the Guilty votes to a bare majority and have the power roles vote Innocent, because the revenge kills a random Guilty voter.

lessons.evidence: Alice protected Carol three nights in a row. Grace blocked Alice on Night 2 and Night 3, and Carol died on Night 3. Alice died that same night still holding 2 medic tokens.

lessons.tip: Before you kill a protected investigator, block the claimed Medic. Agree the holder, target and block in night chat and submit exactly that plan. Kill the info roles whose results can still narrow down your team, such as a Tracker who could see the Katana visit.
lessons.evidence: Frank and Grace agreed every plan word for word in night chat. Grace blocked Alice while Frank killed Erin (Tracker) on Night 2 and Carol (Sheriff) on Night 3. Both kills succeeded, and no Village investigator ever looked at them.

lessons.tip: Let a likely Jester or a chaotic claimant soak up the town's hangs, and back hangs on Village players when it costs you little. Quiet Vanilla claims with no visits leave nothing to contradict. Track the vote math so you know when you have the majority.
lessons.evidence: Frank and Grace claimed Vanilla Villager, voted with the town to hang the Jester, then used their 2-of-3 majority on Day 4 to hang Dave. They won without either of them ever being investigated.

lessons.tip: Count toward parity every Day. With 2 Yakuza among 6 players, one wasted hang plus a night kill can hand them the game. Before agreeing to a hang, ask whether it removes a Katana holder.
lessons.evidence: At 6 alive on Day 3, hanging the Jester, then the Katana kill on Carol and the revenge on Alice that night, left 3 players: Dave and both Yakuza. The game was decided before Day 4's vote.

tips_feedback.tip: Check the rules before calling a contradiction: actions are optional, roles can repeat, and a role-block or swap explains a missing or odd result.
tips_feedback.why: Ignoring it was the first decisive mistake, which shows the tip is correct. Dave named the two-Snipers possibility, ignored it, and shot Heidi, a real Village Sniper.

tips_feedback.tip: Before a hang, ask whether the nominee wants it (self-nominations, reckless lies). If you hang a possible Jester, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority with power roles Innocent, because revenge kills a random Guilty voter.
tips_feedback.why: The town ignored it, and the result proves it right. Bob nominated himself twice and the town hanged him 6-0. The revenge killed Alice, the Medic, which pushed the Village into a lost position.

tips_feedback.tip: Protect the likeliest Katana targets (claimed investigators, vocal analysts) without announcing it or repeating a pattern. After claiming, spend a token on self-protection soon; Medics often die holding both.
tips_feedback.why: The Medic ignored it, and the result proves it right. Alice protected Carol every night, was blocked twice by a Pharmacist who expected it, and died with both tokens.

tips_feedback.tip: Dead players spend nothing: use one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, ritual guess, shots) on the first night they can change a vote or remove a threat, because holders who wait usually die with them.
tips_feedback.why: Players ignored it, and the result proves it right. Dave held his last Sniper shot until he was hanged by the two Yakuza he could have shot, and Alice died holding both medic tokens.

tips_feedback.tip: Confirm the Katana holder and target in night chat and submit exactly that; with two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill.
tips_feedback.why: Frank and Grace agreed and submitted identical plans every night, and both Katana kills plus both Medic blocks went through.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name a corroborated mechanical fit: an Evil read the claim doesn't explain, a broken claim, elimination from a group result.
tips_feedback.why: On Day 2, Alice, Carol and Erin voted Innocent on Dave because of Carol's check corroborated by Erin's track. That saved a Village Sniper from a hang the Yakuza had started.

tips_feedback.tip: Post a result that bears on a vote in your first speech, with night, target and exact result; held-back results look retrofitted.
tips_feedback.why: Carol posted her Dave result first thing on Day 2, and Erin backed it up at once. That made Dave's clear the strongest fact in the game and was what got him acquitted.

issues.description: Day 2: Dave (Standard shot at Heidi) and Heidi (Strong shot at Dave) took their Sniper shots in the same round, so per R25 both should take effect together when the round ends. The program fired Dave's shot first. It killed Heidi, and her shot was then dropped as 'died since taking it', with no 'someone shot at Dave' announcement. The rules don't say how simultaneous round-end day actions are ordered or whether a shooter killed by another round-end action still fires. R25 also says timing shouldn't show whose turn it was, yet the earlier turn's shot won. Treating the shots as simultaneous would have killed Dave too, which changes the game's outcome. Heidi also lost all 3 tokens (told 0 left) for a shot that never fired; that matches R21 but is not spelled out for this case.

The setup note says roles may repeat, but Heidi ('Dave's Sniper claim is false, because I know my own role') and Dave ('I know my own role, so Heidi's Sniper claim was false') each took the other's Sniper claim as proof of lying. Erin and Bob reasoned the same way. Both were real Village Snipers, and this mistake led to one Village player killing another.

Several players (Erin, Alice and others) treated Carol's Not Evil Sheriff result on Dave as putting him 'on the Good side'. Not Evil doesn't settle alignment, because Serial Killers, Arsonists and the Katana holder also read Not Evil to the Sheriff.

Day 4: Dave argued that hanging him would leave the Katana holder to kill the last Village player the next night. That only applies if just one of Frank and Grace was Yakuza. Since both were Yakuza, hanging him ended the game at once (R1).
